story.title: Major U.S. Banks Experience Widespread Online Access Issues
story.summary: Customers at several of the largest U.S. banks, including Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo, are reporting difficulties accessing their online accounts. The issues have been noted across multiple platforms, with many users indicating service outages. This situation has affected a significant number of customers attempting to manage their accounts online.

explore_lenses.label: Was this a cyberattack or a banking-system failure?
explore_lenses.title: Chase cites an internal software bug
explore_lenses.summary: JPMorgan Chase said the disruption stemmed from a temporary software bug in an on-premise hardware system, rather than a cyberattack. The bank characterized the incident as limited to Chase, though transactions involving Chase could be slower elsewhere.

claims.text: JPMorgan Chase spokesperson Joe Evangelisti said the issue was a temporary software bug in an on-premise hardware system and was not cyber-related.
Chase said it was not a systemic banking issue; it said other institutions could experience slower transactions when they were a party to a transaction with Chase.
The public reporting reviewed does not independently establish the technical chain of failure or whether any separate outages at other banks occurred.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The full incident analysis, including the precise hardware and software components involved, had not been released.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Zelle and other banks appear affected?
explore_lenses.title: Shared transactions can transmit delays
explore_lenses.summary: Reports across bank apps did not necessarily mean that every bank’s own systems were down. Zelle and U.S. Bank said their systems were operating, while acknowledging that payments involving affected financial institutions could be delayed.

claims.text: Early Warning Services, which operates Zelle, said the Zelle network was fully operational and that problems at financial institutions could delay payments for some customers.
U.S. Bank said its systems were not directly affected but that customers sending or receiving Zelle payments with another institution could encounter delays.
Zelle is a bank-linked payment network owned by Early Warning Services, whose owners include Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC, Truist, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.

explore_lenses.label: What happens to delayed or disputed payments?
explore_lenses.title: Transactions may need verification after service returns
explore_lenses.summary: Chase said customers retained access to accounts and funds even as some transactions took longer. If a customer later believes an electronic transfer was unauthorized or incorrect, Chase’s account agreement describes an error-resolution process, including potential provisional credit while it investigates.

claims.text: Chase said customers still had access to their accounts and funds while it worked to restore service.

Under Chase’s deposit agreement, customers disputing an electronic-fund-transfer error must generally notify the bank no later than 60 days after the first statement showing the issue; Chase says it will generally determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days.

If Chase needs more time to investigate a qualifying disputed electronic transfer, its agreement says it may take up to 45 days and will provide provisional credit within 10 business days for the amount in question.

story_report.summary: Customers at several major U.S. banks, including Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, reported difficulty accessing online accounts as reports of outages spread across multiple platforms. The disruptions affected customers trying to manage accounts online, while some payments involving other financial institutions could be delayed. JPMorgan Chase attributed its problem to a temporary software bug in an on-premise hardware system and said the incident was not cyber-related, but public reporting did not establish whether other banks’ reported problems had the same cause.

sections.heading: Chase Describes Temporary Software Bug
sections.body: JPMorgan Chase spokesperson Joe Evangelisti said a temporary software bug in an on-premise hardware system caused the Chase issue and was not related to a cyberattack. Chase said the event was not a systemic banking problem, though transactions could move more slowly at other institutions when Chase was a party to them. The company also said customers retained access to their accounts and funds while service was being restored.

sections.heading: Zelle Payments Face Potential Delays
sections.body: Early Warning Services, operator of the Zelle network, said Zelle itself was fully operational, but problems at financial institutions could delay payments for some customers. U.S. Bank said its own systems were not directly affected, while warning that customers sending or receiving Zelle payments involving another institution could encounter delays. Zelle is a bank-linked network operated by Early Warning, whose owners include Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.

sections.heading: Chase Agreement Sets Dispute Process
sections.body: For disputed electronic-fund-transfer errors, Chase’s deposit agreement generally requires customers to notify the bank within 60 days of the first statement showing the issue. Chase says it generally determines whether an error occurred within 10 business days. If more time is needed for a qualifying dispute, the agreement allows up to 45 days for an investigation and provides for provisional credit within 10 business days for the amount at issue.

unresolved.text: A full incident analysis, including the precise hardware and software components involved, had not been released, and public reporting did not independently establish the technical chain of failure or whether separate outages occurred at other banks.

User-reported outage spikes do not by themselves confirm a systemwide failure at every named institution. No public resolution timetable or complete accounting of delayed, reversed or duplicated transactions was available in the reporting reviewed.

related_stories.title: US Air Travel Gradually Normalizes After Three-Day Disruption
related_stories.summary: US air travel is gradually returning to normal following three days of significant disruptions caused by a no-takeoff order from aviation authorities. Over the weekend, many passengers faced chaotic conditions at airports, with reports of stranded travelers waiting for updates and rebooking options.

related_stories.title: Germany Dominates Netherlands 5-0 to Secure Nations League Quarterfinal Spot
related_stories.summary: Germany achieved a commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in their final Group A2 match of the UEFA Nations League. This win, highlighted by two goals from Wirtz, secured Germany's top position in the group and a place in the quarterfinals.
